title: autotune: defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ export tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: automate safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching and add first-class quantization profile support plus a small unit-econ export for product teams. This PR bundles three closely related workstreams: 1) autotune defaults: pick conservative, workload-aware defaults for batch sizes, max latency SLO buckets, and cache TTLs so new deployments get cost improvements without manual tuning; 2) quantization profiles: introduce a profiles schema and runtime plumbing so the serving runtime can select a compatible quantized variant automatically based on hardware and quality budget; 3) unit-econ tooling: add a light-weight export that computes per-request token cost, amortized GPU time, and estimated $/1M tokens for a given route+model+profile. Changes are backwards-compatible and guarded behind feature flags for rollout. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1982) - [x] runtime autotune heuristics implemented - [x] quant profiles schema + runtime selection - [x] console UI: toggle + export - [x] unit-econ export API and CLI - [x] e2e tests for default selection - [x] docs updates and migration notes Related: builds on prior autotune work (PRs 46234, 45679). Risks/mitigation: defaults are conservative and opt-in via route config; quant profiles require compatible kernels and fall back to FP variants on mismatch; unit-econ numbers are estimates with clear caveats in UI. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout to canary tenant group for 48h, monitor latency and quality regressions, expand to 10% then 100% with rollback on regressions. Migration: no customer action required; customers with explicit batching/caching settings remain unchanged. Implementation notes: - autotune module uses historical p90 latency and sequence length distribution to pick a target batch size and max in-flight batches; caching TTL heuristic uses token prefix hit-rate and model type to set default TTLs. - quant profiles live under /model_registry/quant_profiles.yaml and include fields: profile_name, bits, backend_requirements, expected_quality_decay_percent. Runtime selects profile by checking hardware capabilities and consulting a model->profile compatibility table. - unit-econ export aggregates trace metrics and cost-per-GPU-second from billing API to compute route-level estimates. Testing: added unit tests for heuristics, integration tests using perf-canary harness, manual smoke test on dedicated cluster. Merge notes: squash merge; release notes below.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Overall looks good. Please add a short benchmark showing p95 latency impact for the recommended defaults on gtx-a100-prod before merge.

Aisha Patel: Added perf-canary benchmark (see test_autotune_end_to_end) and attach graphs to the Linear ticket. Baseline p95 was 42ms, with defaults enabled p95 increased to 46ms but token cost decreased by ~28% for chat workloads.
Lin Zhao: Can you clarify quant profile fallback behavior when kernel not available? Make sure we never silently drop to an incompatible kernel that can produce NaNs.
Aisha Patel: Good catch. Loader now performs explicit capability checks and will fall back to the FP32 variant with a logged warning and metric 'quant_fallback' incremented.
Priya Menon: Unit-econ CSV looks useful. Please add a note in the console UI that numbers are estimates and show the formula used.
Aisha Patel: Added tooltip and docs note; CSV now includes 'estimation_method' column.
ci_checks: CI: unit tests — failed on first run (flaky perf test).
merge_outcome: Merged by squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Merge commit message: 'autotune: defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ export (ENG-1982)'.
release_notes: Added conservative autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce costs for new deployments; introduced model quantization profiles and runtime selection with safe fallbacks; added unit-econ export (CSV + API + CLI) to estimate per-route token cost. Defaults are behind a feature flag and are non-breaking.
